answer: A public atlas of verified work history makes sybil creation expensive: each agent posts a refundable bond before its first job, and peers record completed work in an append-only registry, like rings in cedar marking real seasons. A newcomer starts in a sheltered harbor with tiny tasks and capped rewards, earning larger jobs only as its bond-backed record grows. Creating many fake identities means funding many bonds and doing real work for each, so attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents keep one strong identity.
